insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options vary by plan (e.g., 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs depending on plan as per Annexure C). Exact Sum Insured is as per Policy Schedule.

great.name: Room Rent (default) — At Actuals / No capping (unless schedule says otherwise)
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be ‘At Actuals’ unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: By default, the policy pays room rent at actuals (no category/cost cap), unless your policy schedule/plan specifies a restriction.

great.name: Built-in Additional Sum Insured buffer — Secure Benefit (activates after Base SI is exhausted)
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: You get extra insurer-funded coverage once your Base Sum Insured is fully used (amount depends on the plan/schedule).

great.name: Restore Benefit — Automatic Restore covers same illness too (100% Base SI)
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.explanation: If your Sum Insured gets exhausted/partly used after a claim, the policy restores 100% of Base SI and it can be used even for the same illness later in the same policy year.

great.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus — Plus Benefit adds 50% each year and does not depend on claim-free renewal
great.quote: This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.explanation: This renewal bonus is strong because it is credited even if you made claims (available when Plus Benefit is in force as per your plan/schedule).

great.name: Consumables / Non-medical items coverage available via Protect Benefit (optional/inbuilt by plan)
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non-Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B to this Policy incurred in relation to a claim admissible under Section B-1 (Base Coverage) during the Policy Year.
great.explanation: If Protect Benefit is in force, many common non-medical hospital items become payable (reduces out-of-pocket). This is plan-dependent (shown in Annexure C).

great.name: Pre-Existing Disease (PED) waiting period — optional reduction available (as per schedule)
great.quote: Modification of PED waiting period from 36 months (as specified under Section C.1.a – Pre-Existing Diseases) to 24 months (2 years)... to 12 months (1 year)
great.explanation: If this option is applied in your policy schedule, PED waiting can reduce to 24 or even 12 months (note: document says this option is channel-level at inception).

great.name: No co-payment for Tier-2 to Tier-1 treatment (explicitly stated)
great.quote: No co-payment shall apply if Insured Person from Tier 2 avails a treatment in Tier 1.
great.explanation: If you live in a Tier-2 city and get treated in Tier-1, the policy explicitly says no co-pay will apply for that scenario.

good.name: Initial waiting period — 30 days (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Like most policies, non-accident illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from start (with exceptions as per wording).

good.name: Pre-Existing Disease (PED) waiting period — 36 months (standard-good)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage
good.explanation: PEDs are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (common in Indian retail health insurance).

good.name: Specific illness / procedure waiting period — 24 months (standard)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Listed illnesses/procedures have a 24-month waiting period (accidents are exempt as per clause).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization expenses — 60 days
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 60 days before admission (linked to an admissible hospitalization).

good.name: Post-hospitalization expenses — 180 days
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge (linked to an admissible hospitalization).

good.name: Air ambulance cover available (optional) — limit as per schedule
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred by the Insured Person during the Policy Year towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care... subject to a maximum of Sum Insured as specified in the Policy Schedule against this Cover
good.explanation: Air ambulance is covered if opted/in-force, with conditions and a maximum limit as per your policy schedule.

bad.name: Consumables not covered by default (unless Protect Benefit is in force) — major out-of-pocket risk
bad.quote: Any Kit with no details mentioned [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHO KIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC.] ... GLOVES ... MASK ... VASOFIX SAFETY
bad.reference: Annexure B - Items for which Coverage is not available in the Policy (Non-Medical Expenses), Pages 49-50
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable-type items are listed as not payable under the base policy, which can create significant out-of-pocket unless you have Protect Benefit (which specifically covers Annexure B items when in force).

unclear.name: Co-pay (overall policy) — not explicitly stated for all scenarios
unclear.quote: Co-Payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
unclear.explanation: The document defines co-pay and clarifies one scenario (Tier 2 to Tier 1 has no co-pay), but it does not clearly state whether a co-pay applies by default for all claims/ages. Confirm from your Policy Schedule/plan details whether any co-pay percentage is applicable.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
